test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 7th December 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: GDP is primarily used to:

options.text: assess the health of a country's economy
assess the literacy rate of the country
assess the foreign policy of the country
assess the health of a country's youth

solution:
The correct answer is __**assess the health of a country's economy.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **GDP** is primarily used to** assess the health of a country's economy.**

 
• The total monetary or consumer value of all finished goods and services produced within the boundaries of a country over a particular period of time is the Gross domestic product (GDP).
 
• GDP offers a country's economic snapshot, used to measure the size of an economy and the pace of growth.
 
• GDP can be measured using** expenditure, production, or income **in three ways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 Measurement of National Income – Income Method

 
 
• Estimated by adding all the factors of production (rent, wages, interest, profit) and the mixed-income of self-employed.
 
• In India, one-third of people are self-employed
 
• This is the ‘domestic’ income, related to the production within the borders of the country
 
 
 
• Measurement of National Income – Production Method
 
 
• Estimated by adding the value added by all the firms.
 
• Value-added = Value of Output – Value of (non-factor) inputs
 

 
 
• This gives GDP at Market Price (MP) – because it includes depreciation (therefore ‘gross’) and taxes (therefore ‘market price’)
 
• To reach National Income (that is, NNP at FC)
 

 
 
• Add Net Factor Income from Abroad: GNP at MP = GDP at MP + NFIA
 
• Subtract Depreciation: NNP at MP = GNP at MP – Dep
 
• Subtract Net Indirect Taxes: NNP at FC = NNP at MP – NIT
 
 
 
• Measurement of National Income – Expenditure Method
 
 
• The expenditure method to measure national income can be understood by the equation given below: 
 
 
• Y = C + I + G + (X-M),
 
• where Y = GDP at MP, C = Private Sector’s Expenditure on final consumer goods, G = Govt’s expenditure on final consumer goods, I = Investment or Capital Formation, X = Exports, I = Imports, X-M = Net Exports
